standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness is local on the source and the target
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-flat-localization}, cited at proof lines 8041-8042
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the claim to flatness of a localised ring map.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Grothendieck criterion: a quotient by a sequence is flat when the sequence maps to a regular sequence in the fibre
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence-general}, cited at proof lines 8043-8045
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the required flatness into a regularity statement in the fibre.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-regularity is preserved when passing to the fibre over the residue field
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the quasi-regular sequence in the fibre of the quotient.

standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-regular sequence in a Noetherian local ring is a regular sequence, and finite modules cut out by a regular sequence are finite free
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades quasi-regularity in the fibre to regularity, which is what the Grothendieck criterion needs.

core_obligations: Reduce to showing that the localised map of quotients is flat (proof lines 8037-8042).
Translate flatness into the requirement that the images of the sequence form a regular sequence in the fibre over the residue field (proof lines 8043-8050).
Use the relative regular immersion lemma to get a quasi-regular sequence in that fibre (proof lines 8051-8054).
Upgrade to a regular sequence by the Noetherian local criterion and conclude (proof lines 8055-8059).
proof_roadmap: Localise and reduce to a regularity statement (proof lines 8037-8050).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that cutting a flat and finitely presented algebra by a sequence whose images are quasi-regular descends flatness from the quotient modulo an ideal with locally nilpotent kernel. The proof reduces flatness to a local statement at primes, converts the required regular sequence condition into a statement about the fibre of the quotient over the residue field, and obtains quasi-regularity of the images in that fibre from the relative regular immersion lemma, after which the Noetherian local criterion upgrades quasi-regularity to regularity and the Grothendieck criterion for regular sequences gives the flatness statement.
